stem: Which of the following solutions of KCl will have the highest value of specific conductance?
solution: The specific conductance increases with concentration, since the number of ions per $\text{cm}^3$ increases with increase of concentration.

stem: Energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous constituent ions is called _____.
solution: Lattice enthalpy is the energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous constituent ions.

stem: In a solid lattice, the cation has left a lattice site and is located at an interstitial position, the lattice defect is:
solution: Frenkel defect is due to dislocation of an ion from its usual lattice site to an interstitial position.

stem:
For the decomposition of azomethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{N}_2\text{CH}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3(g) + \text{N}_2(g)$ a first order reaction, the variation in partial pressure with time at $600$ K is given as shown in the figure.

The half life of the reaction is.
solution:
For a first order reaction

$$k = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{P_0}{P} \Rightarrow \ln\frac{P}{P_0} = -kt$$

Comparing with $y = mx$: $k = -\text{slope} = 3.465 \times 10^{4}$

$$t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{3.465 \times 10^{4}} = 2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{s}$$
notes: temperature partly cut off in image; 600 K assumed

stem: If the radius of the 3rd Bohr's orbit of hydrogen atom is $r_3$ and the radius of 4th Bohr's orbit is $r_4$. Then:
How many elements are there in $6^{th}$ period of periodic table?
Observe the given boundary surface diagrams of two orbitals I and II and choose the correct option.
solution: In boundary surface diagram I the four lobes lie between the $y$ and $z$ axes ($d_{yz}$), whereas in diagram II the four lobes lie on the $x$ and $y$ axes ($d_{x^2-y^2}$).

stem:
Given that $E^\circ_{\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} = +1.23$ V; $E^\circ_{\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}/\text{SO}_4^{2-}} = 2.05$ V; $E^\circ_{\text{Br}_2/\text{Br}^-} = +1.09$ V; $E^\circ_{\text{Au}^{3+}/\text{Au}} = +1.4$ V

The strongest oxidising agent is:
solution: Reduction potential is maximum for $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$; therefore it is the strongest oxidising agent amongst the given species.

stem: Given that bond energies of H $-$ H and Cl $-$ Cl are $430\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $240\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively and $\Delta H_f$ for HCl is $-90\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, bond enthalpy of HCl is
solution:
$\dfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{HCl}$

$\Delta H = \sum \text{B.E. of reactants} - \sum \text{B.E. of products}$

$$-90 = \frac{1}{2}\times 430 + \frac{1}{2}\times 240 - \text{B.E. of HCl}$$

$$\therefore \text{B.E. of HCl} = 215 + 120 + 90 = 425\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

stem: The compounds $[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Br}_2$ and $[\text{PtBr}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Cl}_2$ constitutes a pair of
solution: $[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Br}_2$ and $[\text{PtBr}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Cl}_2$ are ionisation isomers (the counter ion and ligand exchange places).

stem: Which of the following molecules acts as a Lewis acid?
solution: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{B}$ is electron deficient, thus behaves as a Lewis acid.

stem: Thiamine and pyridoxine are also known respectively as:
solution: Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ is also known as thiamine while vitamin $\text{B}_6$ is known as pyridoxine.
